frozen_at: after the H8 refutation, before the H9 readout probe

what_is_refuted.claim: the predicted parent-action context improves low-level skill recognition

what_remains_true.claim: the readout layer is the only independent algorithmic increment: replacing the jointly trained softmax head with a closed-form probe is worth about +1.75 pt (17/17), roughly 26% of the total gain
what_remains_true.numbers: best recorded segF1 0.7385 (4 seeds, sd 0.0029) vs SF 0.6719

the_unit_problem_that_decides_the_design.facts: 17 objects over 5 recording dates; test folds share 85.3% of frames with training (TRAINING_PROTOCOL_AUDIT.md:43); the pairwise test-episode overlap is 75.8 / 86.1; date-level Wilcoxon is p = 0.0625
the_unit_problem_that_decides_the_design.consequence: 17 objects are not 17 independent units. A design that reports 17/17 without a date-grouped or clustered interval overstates the precision; the honest independent count is 5 dates.
the_unit_problem_that_decides_the_design.what_a_correct_answer_must_say: the evaluation unit and the grouping rule, plus the resulting count of independent units

cannot_fix: generalization to unseen objects, sessions or datasets — the sealed set shares all 17 objects and all 5 dates
boundary localization — the existing boundary metrics are dominated by boundaries unrelated to the held-out object (96.7%) and partly on training frames (46.7%), so they cannot measure the claim
the budget confound: every GRU variant trained on 37.6% of SF's frames, so 'temporal modelling is useless' is not separable from 'it was undertrained'
must_not_do: tune on the 37 sealed episodes: they are unread and a one-time read, so they can only be a pre-registered confirmation
propose another architecture sweep — the budget does not cover it and H8 already showed the axis is dead
claim an unseen-object or cross-dataset result
grading: Three scored parts: (1) identifies the refuted claim and the surviving increment with numbers; (2) names 5 dates as the independent unit and gives a grouping rule; (3) states at least two things the change cannot fix. A design that proposes a large sweep scores 0 on cost discipline even if it is scientifically plausible.
